title: Let a 3.3 V pin switch a 20 mA LED
story: A microcontroller pin gives 3.3 V but may only supply 8 mA. You want a red LED at about 20 mA from the 5 V rail, through a 150 ohm resistor. An NPN transistor (beta = 100) does the heavy lifting: the pin only drives its base. Pick the base resistor so the transistor is fully on (saturated) and the pin is safe.
hints: The collector needs about 20 mA, so the base needs at least 20 mA / 100 = 0.2 mA. For a solid switch give it 5 to 10 times more.
The base sits about 0.7 V above ground, so the base resistor sees 3.3 - 0.7 = 2.6 V.
Check both limits: enough base current to saturate, but no more than the pin's 8 mA.
